videos.title: Tired of manually keyframing animations and syncing sound effects? Astra handles fast.
videos.ai_tech_id: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) — agentic AI assistant driving Adobe Premiere
summary: Futurepedia shows GPT-6 Astra taking over a tedious video-editing chore: dropping raw images onto a Premiere timeline and asking Astra to add pop-up and wobble animations, then pointing it at a folder of sound effects and letting it pick what fits.

The workflow is presented in two passes rather than a single generation: a 12-minute first pass to build the animated intro, followed by a 13-minute round of tweaks and SFX searching, for a total of under 25 minutes to reach a polished, ready-to-ship result.

The framing explicitly isn't that AI replaces a human editor, but that the boring keyframe-and-sync busywork can be handed off to an agentic assistant working inside the editor itself, freeing the creator to do something else while it runs.

videos.title: I Tested Opus 5.5 at Every Effort Level. What You Need to Know.
summary: Nate Herk gives Claude Opus 5.5 the identical complex 3D conference prompt six separate times, once at each available effort level: Low, Medium, High, Extra, Max, and Ultracode, to see how output quality scales with compute spend.

For every run he compares the actual output alongside runtime, estimated API-equivalent cost, token usage, verification checks performed, and clarifying questions the model asked, building a timestamped side-by-side of the same creative build at increasing effort.

His headline finding is that the most expensive run was not the best one; he closes by naming the specific effort level he'd actually reach for on a complex creative build like this, giving viewers a practical cost-versus-quality guide for choosing effort settings.

videos.title: How to Connect GPT-6 Astra to DaVinci Resolve With MCP
videos.ai_tech_id: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) via DaVinci Resolve MCP bridge
summary: Sabrina Ramonov demonstrates GPT-6 Astra editing a video from scratch inside DaVinci Resolve itself, using a new DaVinci Resolve MCP bridge that lets the model operate the editor directly instead of just returning editing instructions to follow manually.

She walks through the full setup: install DaVinci Resolve 21.0.3, open Codex and select GPT-6 Astra with reasoning effort set to light, feed it the DaVinci Resolve MCP repository link and let it self-install, restart Resolve, then launch the resolve_bridge script from the Workspace/Scripts menu before handing Astra source photos and an editing request.

She stresses that step order matters (finish MCP setup before restarting Resolve, create the project before launching the bridge script), framing the result as a chat request that becomes real work inside a desktop video editor, with the human still choosing photos and describing intent while Astra executes the edit.

videos.title: 5 Videos to Learn 5 AI Skills
videos.ai_tech_id: General AI literacy curriculum — includes Claude AI, plus AI for money, content, and video generation
summary: Sabrina Ramonov curates a five-video learning path for viewers who feel they keep collecting scattered AI tips without a structured starting point, sequencing the videos from AI basics through monetization, Claude AI specifically, AI content creation, and AI video.

Rather than new demos, this is a playlist-style roundup linking to five of her existing videos in a deliberate order, paired with explicit advice to pick one video at a time, take notes, and apply the lesson to a real project before moving to the next skill.

Her core argument is that depth beats dabbling: watching supplies the input but only hands-on practice on a real problem builds the skill, so she recommends working the list in order or jumping straight to whichever skill is needed for an upcoming project.
